title: Resource Management and Cleanup
learningObjectives: Explain the main concept in this lesson.
Identify how references, state, or lifetime affect behavior.
Trace an example and predict its result.
Choose an appropriate practice for a simple scenario.

understand.concept: Resources such as files, connections, locks, or device handles often need reliable release. Cleanup should occur even when errors happen. Scoped cleanup, finally blocks, or context managers can help, but syntax and guarantees vary across languages.
understand.whyItMatters: Unreleased resources can cause failures even when memory is reclaimed; predictable cleanup improves reliability.
understand.analogy: Borrowed equipment needs to be returned; software cleanup can also involve errors, ownership, and timeouts.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy simplifies software rules; language and runtime behavior may differ.

explain.narrative: Identify the data or resource, who can access it, and how it changes or remains available. Trace the example, and consider what happens after a function returns or when an error interrupts normal flow. Use language-specific lifecycle and ownership rules for real implementations.
